paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Rav Avya [עויא; our version אויא]. Menachot 37b: Rav Avya bar Rav Avya should read Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, and Rabbi Chiyya, as the new editions have it. In Rabbi Assi’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Pesachim 24b. He sat before Rav Assi, Yevamot 117a, and spoke in Rav Assi bar Chanina’s name. He found Rav Ashi’s students, Eruvin 11b. He spoke to Rav Ashi: Nedarim 35a, 51b; Chullin 80a; Pesachim 44b; Bava Batra 82a; Bava Metzia 96a; Eruvin 48b; Nazir 37a; Bava Batra 3a, 46b, 150a. Chapter Klal Gadol 74b: Rif’s Rav Ashi bar Rav Avira is an error, since the Gemara has Rav Acha bar Rav Avya. Bava Kamma 62a: Rav Adda bar Rav Avya speaking to Rav Ashi is an error. He objected to Rav Ashi, Ketubbot 76a. Apparently this Rav Ashi is the early Rav Ashi. Before Rav Chisda, in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Rav Chisda told him, “Who heeds you and your teacher Rabbi Yochanan?”, Pesachim 33b [cited as 30b]. He spoke to Rav Menashe, Chullin 31a.
